Data: [TidyTuesday 2026-07-21](https://github.com/rfordatascience/tidytuesday/tree/main/data/2026/2026-07-21).

The Greyson NDE Scale scores an account out of 32 and treats 7 as the point at which it counts as a near-death experience, so plotting the archive against that threshold asks a plain question of it.
The answer is that 53 of the 587 scored accounts reach 7, about one in eleven, and the whole archive stops at 27 without ever approaching the top of the scale.
Splitting the accounts by the eight themes coded for them changes almost nothing: every row's median falls between 2 and 3, and even `ai_unity`, whose tail clears the threshold most often, does so in only 17% of the accounts that carry it.
Both the score and the theme flags here are derived from the narrative text rather than from an interview, so the figure says more about how the archive was coded than about what the experiences were.
